key_evidence: Portugal's parliament passed a blanket ban on face-concealing clothing in public spaces on 17 July 2026 with a two-thirds majority; fines run from EUR200 to EUR4,000 and forcing another person to wear a face veil carries up to three years' imprisonment.

Amnesty International Portugal's executive director Joao Godinho Martins said the law is discriminatory and a threat to human rights, and Amnesty says removing explicit references to Islam from earlier drafts did not change that it disproportionately affects Muslim women who cover their faces as religious practice.

The bill originated with the far-right Chega party; the final text was reframed around security and public order with specified exceptions, partly to survive constitutional scrutiny under Article 41 of the Portuguese Constitution.

Movement is concentrated in Empathy (-0.6 raw, on Non-Judgment, Perspective-Taking and Cultural Empathy), Equity (-0.3 raw, on Universality and Bias Awareness) and Boundaries (-0.2 raw, on Consent Orientation). The remaining five dimensions move only 0.1 raw each on the integer scoring grid.
No band crossing occurs: Portugal moves from 65.6 to 60.6 and remains Established. Approximately -1.6 of the -5.0 is grid rounding and approximately -3.4 is conduct.

Recommendation is flag-for-review rather than downgrade because the law's human rights characterisation rests on a single tier-3 source (Amnesty International); no treaty body, Council of Europe or Portuguese court assessment exists yet.
